source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watermelon is attacked by insect pests that either transmit disease or feed directly on the plant.

Among insects that act as disease vectors, aphids (a green species and a black species) are the main vectors of the two viral diseases affecting watermelon (Papaya Ring Spot Virus and Watermelon Mosaic Virus), spreading them as they feed on leaves and move between plants.

Among insects that damage the plant directly: a yellow/golden beetle-type pest feeds on young leaves, flowers, and fruit skin, reducing photosynthesis and marring fruit appearance; cutworms attack the stem at the soil surface during the day and can cut down young seedlings, especially soon after transplanting or emergence; cucumber beetles (Cucumber beetles) feed on roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruit and are also implicated in spreading bacterial wilt; and various leaf-feeding and fruit-feeding insects (leaf-rolling caterpillars, leaf miners, and fruit flies) are also mentioned as damaging foliage or reducing fruit quality and marketability.

Recommended control measures include a combination of good cultural practices (crop rotation, use of disease/pest-tolerant varieties, proper field sanitation to remove crop residues and reduce overwintering sites, and correct timing of planting to avoid peak pest periods) together with the judicious use of registered insecticides, applied at recommended rates and following pre-harvest intervals, when pest populations reach damaging levels.
